text:
Roe v. Wade is controversial because it made a deeply contested moral question, when life or personhood begins and how to weigh it against a woman's bodily autonomy, into a nationwide constitutional rule. It did this by finding an implied right to abortion in the Fourteenth Amendment's right to privacy. Critics, including some legal scholars who support abortion rights, called that reasoning weak and an act of judicial overreach, while supporters saw it as protecting reproductive freedom and health, until Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization overturned it in 2022.
